$comment: Campus family (docs/map-briefs/st_johns, steps 7-10: DeKoven Hall's offices, Memorial Hall's library, the chapel, the gym and pool). Parts as in academy.json; parts are only ever added at the end. Edit, then run `node tools/content/setpieces.mjs`.

notes.design: St. John's step 7 (DeKoven Hall, photo 10: dark wood wainscot and door frames, panelled doors with a diamond pattern, framed pictures, a wood plank ceiling; plaques, trophies and the crest in the floor, docs/map-briefs/st_johns). Laid out as the Classroom Bay: two Rooms open to each other and at both ends, the hall down the middle (z 2.8 to 5.2) between walls 0.3 m thick whose lower metre is Walnut (the wainscot) under plaster, each with a 2 m doorway at an office's back (x 1.3 to 3.3) and an open diamond-panelled Oak Door in it; half partitions at the ends, so bays side by side make one hall. Each office 7.9 x 6 m: a Desk, an Office Chair behind it, a tall Bookcase on its west partition. Beamed ceilings, Twin sash windows. Corridor: Trophies and portraits (a Trophy Case and an Honours Board, 1.9 m of hall left for bots), Plain, or Reception (our Crest Roundel at 0.75, the Crest Shield, an Honours Board). Offices: North one shut swaps its furniture and open door for a shut door (St. John's is near its entity limit). One light, in the hall. Props: 11 (display), 9 (plain), 12 (reception); 8 with the north office shut and a plain hall.

notes.design: St. John's step 8 (Memorial Hall, the library: one tall storey, a real library inside, docs/map-briefs/st_johns). Two Tall Halls (two storeys, no column) open to each other and at both ends: solid walls on the ground storey with two wide library Bookcases against each long wall (1.6 m clear of the middle, so the South door's Round arch fits between them), Arched windows (glass) in the storey above, a Beamed roof in dark wood. Two walnut Dining Tables as reading tables down the middle (aisles 2.5 m either side). One light. Props: 6, blocks: none.

pieces.blurb: A round stone porch 6.5 m across under a tall red cone: a doorway in from the south, one on into the hall north, windows east and west (photo 14).

notes.design: St. John's step 8 (photo 14: a low stone building under a tall red conical roof over a round-arched entrance; Q7 its entrance faces east / north-east to the grounds). The Round Porch tile (a round room, 2.6 m doorways south and north, windows east and west, a flat roof on the wall at 4 m) under the red Cone Roof at scale 2.1 (7.1 m across, 9.7 m tall, its top 13.7 m up). Put it against a Library Bay whose South door is a Round arch, turned so its south door faces the grounds. Turns only (the round wall's pieces are not their own mirror image). Two parts: one prop, one light.

notes.design: St. John's step 9 (the chapel, photos 11, 13, 21, 22: tall arched stained windows between buttresses, low side aisles behind arcades, dark wood pews either side of a centre aisle, a dark timber roof; docs/map-briefs/st_johns). Two Tall Halls across the nave (16 m), open to each other and at both ends: their long walls solid both storeys in the look's stone, the Collegiate facade's buttresses at each bay's ends and its battlements on top, a Beamed roof in dark wood. A Stained Glass Window (2.2 x 6.1 m, drawn on both faces of the wall: it is solid behind) in the middle of each long wall from 1.9 m up. An arcade 2.1 m in from each wall (a pier at each end of the bay, half of one where bays meet, and a stone lintel at 2.8 to 3.6 m) makes the side aisles (2.1 m clear: bots walk them). Two Pew Rows (seven pews each, one prop) face east either side of a centre aisle 2 m wide. Bays in a row make the nave; the Chapel Narthex goes at the west end, the Chapel Chancel at the east. One light. Parts as placed: 6 blocks, 4 props, 1 light.

pieces.blurb: A chapel's east end: the chancel arch, steps up to the altar before its reredos, a rose window high in the end wall, the organ in a vestry north with a door out, a sacristy south with the back door.

notes.design: St. John's step 9 (photo 11: a great round arch before the chancel, a round stained-glass rose window high in the end wall, the altar; the owner: behind the altar a room and an office, reached from the back or from a door at the end of the left aisle before the altar steps; the right aisle's end door leads outside). Two Tall Halls, their east wall solid. Across the west side a wall 0.6 m thick with the chancel opening in its middle (6 m wide, 6.4 m high: a stone band over it) and a 2 m doorway at the end of each side aisle (the Chapel Nave Bay's aisles). Inside: the sanctuary in the middle, two white marble steps up (0.5 m), the Altar before its reredos against the east wall, the Rose Window over it; south of it the sacristy (a Desk and an Office Chair) behind a 4 m wall, the back door in the south wall; north of it the vestry with the Pipe Organ and a door out in the north wall. Two lights. Parts: 9 blocks, 5 props, 2 lights. (The basement stair the owner describes is left for the map: the kit has no stair down yet.)

pieces.blurb: A chapel's west end: red doors in the end wall under a rose window, a spiral stone stair each side of the way in, up to a gallery over the entrance that looks down the nave.

notes.design: St. John's step 9 (the owner: when you first come in, a spiral cobble staircase on the left and on the right up to the upper seating, the gallery over the entrance from which photo 21 was taken; photo 22: red double doors in the end wall under a great window). Two Spiral Stairs, the south one as it comes, the north one turned half round, so their shafts stand against the outer walls and both their doors face the way in: a passage 2 m wide from the red doors (a 2 m doorway in the middle of the west wall, an open Painted Door in it) to the nave, the stairs' doors either side of it. Upstairs, the stairs' floors make the gallery over the entrance (between the shafts and over the passage), a railing along its east edge over the nave. A Rose Window (amber) over the doors. Turns only (a spiral stair is not its own mirror image). Two lights. Parts: 3 blocks, 2 props, 2 lights.

notes.design: St. John's step 10 (Farrand Hall gym, photos 2 and 3: a full basketball court under a long arched truss roof, rows of hanging lights, glass-block windows down both long walls, bleacher-height brick side walls, a maple floor). Three Tall Halls across (24 m), open to each other and at both ends, Ceiling Open: the Vault Bay (truss) roofs them (boards under a sheet roof springing at 8 m, rising 2.3 m; its truss's four pendant lamps). Old Brick walls, the Brick facade; the ground storey's long walls solid, Twin windows (glass) in the storey above (frosted when cracked, if the look's glass is reinforced). Oak Planks floor; lay a Basketball Court Lines prop over three or four bays. Bleachers (four tiers, walked up as stairs) against either wall. East end Closed puts a brick wall across the east end with a Basketball Hoop (wall) on it and the vault's end variant over it (its gable) (turn the bay half round for a closed west end). Parts as placed: 1 prop (the vault) and a light; bleachers 1 or 2 more, the hoop 1. The Gym Entrance is the west end.

pieces.blurb: A gym's entrance end, 24 m across: a one-storey brick wall with a wide doorway in its middle, a balcony with a rail over it (ladders up at each end), our crest on the wall above, the vault's gable.

notes.design: St. John's step 10 (photo 2: a brick end wall about one storey high under the barrel-vault roof, a double-door opening in its middle to a lit corridor, a balcony rail above the brick; Q9: the entrance is the west end). As the Gym Bay, its west side walled: a Wide doorway in the middle cell's ground storey, brick both storeys. A balcony 3 m deep along the wall at 4 m over the doors (a wood slab, a steel rail along its edge), a ladder up at each end (the rail stops short of them); the Vault Bay's end variant closes the vault's gable over the wall; our Crest Shield on the wall above the balcony (banners of our own, Q12). Parts: 2 blocks, 2 ladders, 2 props, 1 light.

pieces.blurb: An indoor pool 22 x 10 m with four lanes, its water 1.4 m deep below a tiled deck all round; brick walls, a band of windows, steps up from a door in the south end.

notes.design: St. John's step 10 (Gerber Pool: its own wing running north-south off the gym's east end; the old map's water 19 x 39 m with a ladder). Eight Tall Halls, 16 x 32 m, Old Brick walls with Twin windows (glass) in the upper storey down both long sides, a flat roof. The pool is the hall's floor (Pool Tiles) inside a tiled deck 1.5 m high round it (2.5 m wide along the sides, 6 m at the south end, 3 m at the north), so it needs no hole in the ground and works on any map; Water fills the basin 1.4 m deep (22 x 10 m) and Pool Lanes (four lanes, three floating ropes) lie in it. In at the south door (a Doorway in the south-west cell) onto a landing at the floor (2 x 3 m, the deck's face ahead), six steps up east from it onto the south deck; a ladder out of the water at the north end. Bots walk the deck all round. Parts: 11 blocks, water, a ladder, 1 prop, 2 lights. Water is a set piece part only shipped pieces have (map/schema.ts).

notes.design: St. John's step 7b (DeKoven's "Reception" on its court face: PLAN_2026-11-12.md 3.3). As the Classroom Entry Bay is to the Classroom Bay: the south half of an Admin Bay is a reception hall 8 m across under a Round arch (3.2 m) in the outer wall (the hall's walls the look's stone inside and out, as the Classroom Entry Bay's: the arch wears no facade), open to the corridor through a 6 m opening between two short piers with the corridor's walnut wainscot. Our own Crest Roundel (2.25 m) is in the corridor's floor facing the way in, the Crest Shield on the corridor's north wall opposite it; a Trophy Case stands against the hall's west partition, an Honours Board hangs on the east one, a Desk and an Office Chair stand east of the way through. The north office and its Offices option as the Admin Bay's. Turn it half round for a way in on the other side; an Admin Bay goes over it on the floor above.

notes.design: St. John's step 8b (Memorial Hall, the library, to the owner's direction: two storeys, alcoves on the ground floor as in one interior photo, rows upstairs under the open roof as in the other; docs/map-briefs/st_johns, OWNER_NOTES_2026-11-21). Ground storey: two Rooms open to each other and at both ends, fieldstone walls (the stone role), a ceiling of pale plaster (the upper floor's underside) with three dark beams across it; four Bookcase Presses standing out 3 m from the long walls, 4 m apart, each with its bench and reading ledge in the alcove west of it; a square Leaded Window in the middle alcove of each wall, its sill 1 m up; a Worn Rug and the Globe in the middle (4.5 m of floor either side of it); two Hanging Lanterns. Upper storey: two Rooms with no roof (ceiling Open), their walls hung with tiles as shingles (Clay Roof Tiles, tinted; a wall of one material shows it on both faces, so inside a pale plaster lining 2.35 m high stands against each, up to the windows' sills); the Ridge Roof Bay over them at the walls' top (its foot 1.8 m under it), two trusses a bay; four Double-sided Bookcases in two rows either side of a 4 m aisle with the Carpet Runner down it (2.3 m of floor between a row and its wall); two wide Leaded Windows a wall, tight under the eaves and close together; two lanterns hung from the trusses. Arch porch (the owner's exterior photo: the arch stands in the ground storey's own wall, the upper storey and its windows run on above it, the porch is a recess into the building): that wall's side is left open and built as blocks stepped behind the Parabolic Stone Arch's band (the opening 4.5 m wide at the ground, 3.15 m at the crown), the game's own crest on the crown; behind it Dark Wood Panels close a porch 6 m wide and 3 m deep with a 2 m doorway on into the library; that wall's two presses and its window are left out. Lights: two, and one in the porch. The roof collides as nothing: nobody reaches it, a grenade thrown high leaves through it.

pieces.displayName: Library End Bay (two storeys, spiral stair)
pieces.blurb: The closed west end of a two-storey library: a spiral stair in a round stone drum in the south corner, alcoves along the north wall, bookcases and the runner upstairs under the open timber roof; our crest on a truss.

notes.design: St. John's step 8b (the owner: two levels, spiral stairs to go up and down; docs/map-briefs/st_johns). The Library Bay (two storeys)'s west end: the Spiral Stair tile in the south cell, its shaft against the south wall and its doors north on both floors (its own sides left open: the outer walls there are four blocks, fieldstone below and shingles above, since a two-level tile's walls are one material), a Room north of it on each storey with walls north and west; the Ridge Roof Bay's end variant (its gable over the west wall). Ground: two Bookcase Presses on the north wall, square Leaded Windows north, west (two) and south (two, in the wall behind the stair's drum: they show outside only), a rug before the stair's door, a lantern. Upstairs: two Double-sided Bookcases along the north side, the runner, wide Leaded Windows in pairs north, south and west, two lanterns; the game's own crest (the Crest Shield) on the east truss's collar, facing the hall. Turns only (the stair is not its own mirror image). Two lights. Blocks 4.

notes.design: St. John's step 8b (the owner's photo of Memorial Hall: a many-sided two-storey body, fieldstone with pale-surrounded square windows and a pale band course below, dark red-brown shingles with a band of wide cream-framed windows above, under a tall steep faceted shingle roof with a flared eave and a small metal cap, a lower roof over the long body behind, a big pale arch in the ground storey's wall beside the faceted end; docs/map-briefs/st_johns). The octagon's whole square, 16 by 16 m: its south half is the Library Bay (two storeys) turned so the hall runs north-south (its parts, part for part; Arch porch: west or east), its north half the Faceted Hall End (spiral stair) tile. The Faceted Spire's hall variant stands on the walls' top centred on the octagon's centre (the middle of the square), cut away where the bay's Ridge Roof Bay runs in under it: inside, the two roofs are one space. A square Leaded Window in every face of the ground storey (two in the north face, one in each diagonal face and each side wall); two wide Leaded Windows in each of the three upper faces and one in each side wall, close under the eave. The stair's drum stands in the middle of the end: the hall's aisle and the runner upstairs lead to its door on both floors, a passage 4 m wide goes round it each side on the ground floor (a rug and a lantern in each), the upper floor is open to the spire. Turns only.

pieces.blurb: A small wing in pale stucco, 5 by 6 m, under a steep roof with swept eaves that tucks in under a taller building's eave: a half-timbered gable north with a red door up three concrete steps and a black handrail.

notes.design: St. John's step 8b (the owner's photo: on the right of the library's faceted end a small wing about 5 m wide in pale stucco with a little half-timber in its gable, its steep roof with a swept, kicked-out eave tucked in under the main roof's eave; a red door up a few concrete steps with a black handrail; a tall narrow window on its side; docs/map-briefs/st_johns). Blocks, no tile (it is narrower than a cell): a concrete base 0.6 m high, plaster walls 0.3 m thick and 3.2 m high round a room 4.4 by 5.4 m, a 2 m doorway in the north wall with an open red Painted Door, three concrete steps of 0.15 m and a black handrail (two posts and a sloped rail) before it. The Swept Gable Roof on the walls' top: its ridge 7.3 m up (under an 8 m eave), its half-timbered gable north; its south end is open (it goes against the taller building's wall). It stands in the cell's west and south part (x -3 to 2, z -4 to 2), against the cell's south side. A tall narrow window in its east wall (two small Leaded Windows, one over the other), a rug and a Bookcase inside, a lantern and a light. Blocks 13, props 6, lights 1.
